column.text: Bitcoin is currently bleeding despite a massive $314 million day of institutional ETF inflows because the market has entered a violent long squeeze fueled by overextended technicals. The dominant narrative today is decoupling from Nasdaq, with crypto correlation dropping to just 0.10 while Solana tumbles another four percent following net liquidations exceeding sixty-five million dollars in longs versus only ten million for shorts. This divergence confirms that price action is being dictated purely by forced selling mechanics rather than fundamental weakness or lack of demand. While stablecoin supply expansion provides a theoretical dry powder floor, the overextended daily RSI readings across major caps and negative twenty-four hour MACD histograms indicate genuine momentum exhaustion that cannot be ignored lightly. Dollar liquidity contracts as macro headwinds intensify with national debt surpassing forty trillion dollars, forcing risk assets to push against an increasingly hostile tide where failed rallies offer better odds than blind continuation plays. The tape remains technically up-trending in a Risk-On regime, yet traders must demand higher proof on any long entry given the structural pressure building beneath the surface. Institutional accumulation at these dips is evident through spot flows and BlackRock completing five billion dollars in tax-deferred swaps, but retail sentiment has not caught up to this reality yet as fear indices hover near greed territory despite the carnage. The market will likely continue grinding lower until liquidation cascades stabilize or a genuine catalyst forces a reversion of mean momentum that current technicals do not support.
